verses.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖν Ἀμπελῶνα ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν
verses.transliteration: Kai ērxato autois en parabolais lalein Ampelōna anthrōpos ephyteusen kai periethēken phragmon kai ōryxen hypolēnion kai ōkodomēsen pyrgon kai exedeto auton geōrgois kai apedēmēsen
verses.literal: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables A man planted a vineyard He put a wall around it dug a wine vat and built a watchtower Then he rented it out . . . to some tenants and went away on a journey

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος
verses.transliteration: Kai apesteilen pros tous geōrgous tō kairō doulon hina para tōn geōrgōn labē apo tōn karpōn tou ampelōnos
verses.literal: At harvest time he sent a servant to the tenants to collect - his share of the fruit of the vineyard

verses.original: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν
verses.transliteration: kai labontes auton edeiran kai apesteilan kenon
verses.literal: But they seized the servant beat him and sent him away empty-handed

verses.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον κἀκεῖνον ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ἠτίμασαν
verses.transliteration: Kai palin apesteilen pros autous allon doulon kakeinon ekephaliōsan kai ētimasan
verses.literal: Then he sent them another servant and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully

verses.original: καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες
verses.transliteration: kai allon apesteilen kakeinon apekteinan kai pollous allous hous men derontes hous de apoktennontes
verses.literal: He sent still another and this one they killed He sent many others some they beat and others they killed

verses.original: Ἔτι ἕνα εἶχεν υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου
verses.transliteration: Eti hena eichen huion agapēton apesteilen auton eschaton pros autous legōn hoti Entrapēsontai ton huion mou
verses.literal: Finally having one beloved son he sent him to them They will respect my son he said

verses.original: Ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία
verses.transliteration: Ekeinoi de hoi geōrgoi pros heautous eipan hoti Houtos estin ho klēronomos deute apokteinōmen auton kai hēmōn estai hē klēronomia
verses.literal: But the tenants said to one another This is the heir Come let us kill him and the inheritance will be ours

verses.original: καὶ λαβόντες ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος
verses.transliteration: kai labontes apekteinan auton kai exebalon auton exō tou ampelōnos
verses.literal: So they seized the son killed him and threw him out of the vineyard

verses.original: Τί οὖν ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις
verses.transliteration: Ti oun poiēsei ho kyrios tou ampelōnos eleusetai kai apolesei tous geōrgous kai dōsei ton ampelōna allois
verses.literal: What then will the owner of the vineyard do He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others

verses.original: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες Οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας
verses.transliteration: oude tēn graphēn tautēn anegnōte Lithon hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes Houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias
verses.literal: Have you never read this Scripture The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone

verses.original: Παρὰ Κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη Καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: Para Kyriou egeneto hautē Kai estin thaumastē en ophthalmois hēmōn
verses.literal: This is from the Lord and it is marvelous in our eyes

verses.original: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον
verses.transliteration: Kai ezētoun auton kratēsai kai ephobēthēsan ton ochlon egnōsan gar hoti pros autous tēn parabolēn eipen kai aphentes auton apēlthon
verses.literal: At this the leaders sought to arrest Jesus for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them But fearing the crowd they left Him and went away

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ
verses.transliteration: Kai apostellousin pros auton tinas tōn Pharisaiōn kai tōn Hērōdianōn hina auton agreusōsin logō
verses.literal: Later they sent - some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάσκεις ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν
verses.transliteration: kai elthontes legousin autō Didaskale oidamen hoti alēthēs ei kai ou melei soi peri oudenos ou gar blepeis eis prosōpon anthrōpōn all’ ep’ alētheias tēn hodon tou Theou didaskeis exestin dounai kēnson Kaisari ē ou dōmen ē mē dōmen
verses.literal: Teacher they said . . . we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one Indeed You are impartial . . . . . . . . . and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not Should we pay them or not

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί με πειράζετε φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω
verses.transliteration: Ho de eidōs autōn tēn hypokrisin eipen autois Ti me peirazete pherete moi dēnarion hina idō
verses.literal: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said Why are you testing Me Bring Me a denarius to inspect

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Καίσαρος
verses.transliteration: hoi de ēnenkan kai legei autois Tinos hē eikōn hautē kai hē epigraphē Hoi de eipan autō Kaisaros
verses.literal: So they brought it and He asked them Whose image is this And whose inscription Caesar’s - they answered

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ Καὶ ἐξεθαύμαζον ἐπ’ αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous eipen autois Ta Kaisaros apodote Kaisari kai ta tou Theou tō Theō Kai exethaumazon ep’ autō
verses.literal: Then Jesus told them Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s And they marveled at Him

verses.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες
verses.transliteration: Kai erchontai Saddoukaioi pros auton hoitines legousin anastasin mē einai kai epērōtōn auton legontes
verses.literal: Then the Sadducees who say there is no resurrection came to Jesus and questioned Him

verses.original: Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Didaskale Mōusēs egrapsen hēmin hoti ean tinos adelphos apothanē kai katalipē gynaika kai mē aphē teknon hina labē ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika kai exanastēsē sperma tō adelphō autou
verses.literal: Teacher Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him

verses.original: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα
verses.transliteration: hepta adelphoi ēsan kai ho prōtos elaben gynaika kai apothnēskōn ouk aphēken sperma
verses.literal: Now there were seven brothers The first one married . . . and died leaving no children

verses.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν καὶ ἀπέθανεν μὴ καταλιπὼν σπέρμα καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως
verses.transliteration: kai ho deuteros elaben autēn kai apethanen mē katalipōn sperma kai ho tritos hōsautōs
verses.literal: Then the second one married the widow but he also died . . . and left no children And the third did likewise

verses.original: καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα ἔσχατον πάντων καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν
verses.transliteration: kai hoi hepta ouk aphēkan sperma eschaton pantōn kai hē gynē apethanen
verses.literal: In this way none of the seven left any children And last of all the woman died

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα
verses.transliteration: en tē anastasei hotan anastōsin tinos autōn estai gynē hoi gar hepta eschon autēn gynaika
verses.literal: In the resurrection then . . . whose . . . wife will she be For all seven were married to her

verses.original: Ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ephē autois ho Iēsous Ou dia touto planasthe mē eidotes tas graphas mēde tēn dynamin tou Theou
verses.literal: Jesus said to them Aren’t you mistaken . . . because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God

verses.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται ἀλλ’ εἰσὶν ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: hotan gar ek nekrōn anastōsin oute gamousin oute gamizontai all’ eisin hōs angeloi en tois ouranois
verses.literal: When the dead rise . . . . . . they will neither marry nor be given in marriage Instead they will be like the angels in heaven

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ Βάτου πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς λέγων Ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰακώβ
verses.transliteration: Peri de tōn nekrōn hoti egeirontai ouk anegnōte en tē biblō Mōuseōs epi tou Batou pōs eipen autō ho Theos legōn Egō ho Theos Abraam kai ho Theos Isaak kai ho Theos Iakōb
verses.literal: But concerning the dead rising have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses how God told him I am the God of Abraham the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν Θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων πολὺ πλανᾶσθε
verses.transliteration: ouk estin Theos nekrōn alla zōntōn poly planasthe
verses.literal: He is not the God of the dead but of the living You are badly mistaken

verses.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν Ποία ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων
verses.transliteration: Kai proselthōn heis tōn grammateōn akousas autōn syzētountōn idōn hoti kalōs apekrithē autois epērōtēsen auton Poia estin entolē prōtē pantōn
verses.literal: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate Noticing how well Jesus had answered them he asked Him Which commandment is the most important of all

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅτι Πρώτη ἐστίν Ἄκουε Ἰσραήλ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Κύριος εἷς ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Apekrithē ho Iēsous Hoti Prōtē estin Akoue Israēl Kyrios ho Theos hēmōn Kyrios heis estin
verses.literal: Jesus replied This is the most important Hear O Israel the Lord our God the Lord is One

verses.original: καὶ ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου
verses.transliteration: kai agapēseis Kyrion ton Theon sou ex holēs tēs kardias sou kai ex holēs tēs psychēs sou kai ex holēs tēs dianoias sou kai ex holēs tēs ischyos sou
verses.literal: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength

verses.original: δευτέρα αὕτη Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν
verses.transliteration: deutera hautē Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton meizōn toutōn allē entolē ouk estin
verses.literal: The second is this Love your neighbor as yourself No other commandment is greater than these

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς Καλῶς Διδάσκαλε ἐπ’ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autō ho grammateus Kalōs Didaskale ep’ alētheias eipes hoti heis estin kai ouk estin allos plēn autou
verses.literal: Right Teacher the scribe replied . . . You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him

verses.original: καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν
verses.transliteration: kai to agapan auton ex holēs tēs kardias kai ex holēs tēs syneseōs kai ex holēs tēs ischyos kai to agapan ton plēsion hōs heauton perissoteron estin pantōn tōn holokautōmatōn kai thysiōn
verses.literal: and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength and to love your neighbor as yourself This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι
verses.transliteration: Kai ho Iēsous idōn auton hoti nounechōs apekrithē eipen autō Ou makran ei apo tēs basileias tou Theou kai oudeis ouketi etolma auton eperōtēsai
verses.literal: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely He said . . . You are not far from the kingdom of God And no one dared to question Him any further

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous elegen didaskōn en tō hierō Pōs legousin hoi grammateis hoti ho Christos huios Dauid estin
verses.literal: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts - He asked How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David

verses.original: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου
verses.transliteration: autos Dauid eipen en tō Pneumati tō Hagiō Eipen Kyrios tō Kyriō mou Kathou ek dexiōn mou Heōs an thō tous echthrous sou Hypokatō tōn podōn sou
verses.literal: Speaking by the Holy Spirit David himself declared The Lord said to my Lord Sit at My right hand until . . . I put Your enemies under . . . Your feet

verses.original: Αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν Κύριον καὶ πόθεν αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός Καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως
verses.transliteration: Autos Dauid legei auton Kyrion kai pothen autou estin huios Kai ho polys ochlos ēkouen autou hēdeōs
verses.literal: David himself calls Him Lord So how can He be David’s son And the large crowd listened to Him with delight

verses.original: Καὶ ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς
verses.transliteration: Kai en tē didachē autou elegen Blepete apo tōn grammateōn tōn thelontōn en stolais peripatein kai aspasmous en tais agorais
verses.literal: In His teaching Jesus also said Watch out for the scribes They like to walk around in long robes to receive greetings in the marketplaces

verses.original: καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις
verses.transliteration: kai prōtokathedrias en tais synagōgais kai prōtoklisias en tois deipnois
verses.literal: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets

verses.original: οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα
verses.transliteration: hoi katesthiontes tas oikias tōn chērōn kai prophasei makra proseuchomenoi houtoi lēmpsontai perissoteron krima
verses.literal: They defraud widows of their houses and for a show make lengthy prayers . . . These men will receive greater condemnation

verses.original: Καὶ καθίσας κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά
verses.transliteration: Kai kathisas katenanti tou gazophylakiou etheōrei pōs ho ochlos ballei chalkon eis to gazophylakion kai polloi plousioi eballon polla
verses.literal: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury He watched the crowd putting money into it And many rich people put in large amounts

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης
verses.transliteration: kai elthousa mia chēra ptōchē ebalen lepta dyo ho estin kodrantēs
verses.literal: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον
verses.transliteration: Kai proskalesamenos tous mathētas autou eipen autois Amēn legō hymin hoti hē chēra hautē hē ptōchē pleion pantōn ebalen tōn ballontōn eis to gazophylakion
verses.literal: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said Truly I tell you this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury

verses.original: πάντες γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑστερήσεως αὐτῆς πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν ἔβαλεν ὅλον τὸν βίον αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: pantes gar ek tou perisseuontos autois ebalon hautē de ek tēs hysterēseōs autēs panta hosa eichen ebalen holon ton bion autēs
verses.literal: For they all contributed out of their surplus but she out of her poverty has put in all . . . she had to live on
